summary: The formula unification this item asks for is DONE and now independently verified end to end. ONE model - airmassForTrueAltitude in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart, Pickering 2002 at h>=10 deg, Young 1994 below it to the horizon, null below the horizon or non-finite, no clamp - is reached by every publishing Dart consumer (AAVSO exporter, in-app calibration wizard, headless host handler for the same wizard driven from a tablet, automatic science pipeline), and mirrors skotiq_imaging::calculate_airmass constant for constant so the FITS card and the Dart surfaces are the same function. AstronomyCalculations.airmass is the one legitimate divergence and is a documented CONVENTION (infinity below the horizon for target scoring) layered over the same model, not a second model. Both owned call sites were severed and confirmed to break. This round closed the one airmass surface still unpinned - the multi-frame 'Airmass span' the wizard PRINTS to the user, which no single-frame test could reach - and corrected two claims in the owned files that I proved are not guaranteed. A FIFTH implementation and the input-side root cause remain, both outside ownership.

revert_check:
TWO severs run this round, both at the production call site, both restored and re-verified green.
(1) star_matching.dart: replaced
      final airmass = recordedAltitudeDeg == null ? null : airmassForTrueAltitude(recordedAltitudeDeg);
    (plus its null guard) with the retired Kasten&Young block ending `airmass = airmass.clamp(1.0, 8.0);`. All 4 wizard tests failed. The NEW span test failed on the rendered widget text first: Expected exactly one matching candidate / Actual: Found 0 widgets with text containing 'Airmass span 10.74' - the wizard printed 6.85 instead. The three pre-existing tests failed with airmass 8.0 vs 11.897103803441906 and with unknown/sub-horizon frames silently reaching the fit at X=1.0.
(2) aavso_export_service.dart: replaced
      final airmass = altitudeDeg == null ? null : airmassForTrueAltitude(altitudeDeg);
    with the retired inline Pickering block ending `final airmass = (1.0 / sinAlt).clamp(1.0, 40.0);`. aavso_export_airmass_test.dart failed: Expected '11.897' Actual '12.360'.
The severs cut the WIRING, not a helper argument: both tests drive the production path (AavsoExportService.exportSession against a real in-memory DB, reading the AMASS field out of the file that would be uploaded; the wizard widget from the frame list through Match Stars, reading the rendered status text and the ScienceFrameContext handed to the backend).
still_broken: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/cockpit_sky_context.dart:182-190 `_airmass()` - a FIFTH implementation: plain secant 1/cos(z), rendered as 'Airmass' on the Dashboard Sky Context panel for the target being imaged right now. 4% high at 10 deg (5.76 vs 5.53) and it prints an em dash below 3 deg where the model gives a real number, so the Dashboard and the frame's own header disagree about the same target. airmass_single_implementation_test.dart does NOT catch it: the detector fingerprints the three named formulas by their constants and a secant has no constants. The file was being edited by another agent (mtime 3 minutes before I looked), so I did not touch it.

native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs - the INPUT-side asymmetry, and the reason the exporter's old comment was untrue. build_rich_header sets `header.altitude = frame_ctx.mount_altitude_deg.or_else(|| pointing.and_then(|p| p.altitude_deg))`, i.e. the FITS AIRMASS card gets a fallback altitude derived from the frame's own pointing plus the app-settings site (context_altitude_pointing). FrameCaptureMetadata::from(&FrameContext) (sequencer/src/scheduling/frame_context.rs:348) copies ctx.mount_altitude_deg verbatim with no fallback, and that is what becomes captured_images.mountAltitude. So in the configuration the Rust comment itself calls 'entirely ordinary' - a run started before the location reached the executor - the frame ships with an AIRMASS card while its DB row has a null altitude, and every Dart consumer then reports 'unknown' for a frame the product demonstrably measured. I deliberately did NOT paper over this in my two files: adding a second altitude derivation to the exporter and the wizard is exactly how this function got four copies.

native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/fits.rs:1303 - comment still claims Young 1994 gives 'X ~ 38.0' at h=0. It gives 31.74; 38 is the Kasten&Young number. Comment-only, but this is the function every other file cites as the reference.
notes: Verified numerically that the Rust and Dart halves agree rather than trusting the 'mirrors' comment: re-implementing fits.rs::calculate_airmass constant for constant reproduces the Dart test pins exactly - 1.154058 at 60 deg, 2.900143 at 20, 11.897104 at 4, 31.734862 at the horizon, and a 0.0395 step at the 10 deg Pickering/Young handover.

The multi-frame span test needed real machinery to reach the readout - the catalog is built by inverting the wizard's own GnomonicProjection so every detection finds a counterpart - because the span is only rendered after matching completes. Every earlier test stopped at the value handed to the backend, which is why the printed number was unpinned.

Complete inventory taken across Dart, Rust, JS/TS and Python: the only airmass arithmetic left outside the canonical function is cockpit_sky_context.dart. altitude_chart.dart's clamp(1, 5) is a plot Y-range on top of AstronomyCalculations.airmass, not a model.
